newsitem.title: USA: 3Com CEO says merger won't change its focus.
newsitem.headline: 3Com CEO says merger won't change its focus.

text.p: 3Com Corp President and Chief Executive Eric Benhamou on Thursday said the company's focus on new computer-networking technology would not change after its merger with modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp.

"Don't expect this merger to cause a radical departure in our direction," Benhamou told hundreds of 3Com customers at a conference in San Francisco. "I want to forewarn you that the strategy is not very much different than the strategy I explained to you a year ago."

On Wednesday, shareholders of Santa Clara, California-based 3Com and Skokie, Illinois-based U.S. Robotics approved the $8.5 billion stock merger of the two companies. Each U.S. Robotics share will be exchanged for 1.75 shares of 3Com stock in a deal expected to close Thursday.
Benhamou described the combination of 3Com and U.S. Robotics as a "growth company." He said 3Com has grown faster than the market overall in recent years "and that trend is continuing."

Benhamou said the new 3Com would provide "end-to-end" computer connectivity. 3Com, a leader in computer networking, brings local area network technology to the combination, while U.S. Robotics will provide wide area network products.

In addition, he said one of the company's strategies would be to use the Internet more to distribute products, and provide World Wide Web-based platforms. U.S. Robotics, for example, currently provides modem upgrades via its Web site.
While Benhamou said the new 3Com would strive to provide open architectures, he said it would also seek intellectual property ownership of all of its products.
3Com will continue to focus on the worldwide market, he said. The combined company will have more than 13,000 employees in some 45 countries.
